title: Left and Right Sum Differences
description:
# Left and Right Sum Differences

Given a **0-indexed** integer array `nums`, build an array `answer` of the same length.

For every index `i`:

*   `leftSum[i]` is the sum of all elements strictly before `i`.
*   `rightSum[i]` is the sum of all elements strictly after `i`.
*   `answer[i] = |leftSum[i] - rightSum[i]|`.

If one side has no elements, its sum is `0`.

Return the array `answer`.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [10,4,8,3]
**Output:** [15,1,11,22]
**Explanation:** The left sums are [0,10,14,22] and the right sums are [15,11,3,0], so the absolute differences are [15,1,11,22].

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1]
**Output:** [0]
**Explanation:** There are no elements on either side of the only index.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 1000`
*   `0 <= nums[i] <= 100000`

solutions.name: Brute Force Separate Sides
solutions.description:
## Approach

For each index, separately add all values on its left and all values on its right, then store the absolute difference.

## Key Insight

The definition of the answer is local to each index, so the most direct baseline is to recompute both side sums from the original array.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Prefix And Suffix Arrays
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a prefix array where `left[i]` is the sum before `i`, and a suffix array where `right[i]` is the sum after `i`. Then compare the two arrays at each index.

## Key Insight

Once every left-side and right-side sum is precomputed, each answer cell can be produced in constant time without rescanning the input.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Rolling Total Balance
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compute the total sum once. During a left-to-right scan, keep a rolling `leftSum` and derive `rightSum` as `total - leftSum - nums[i]`.

## Key Insight

At any index, the whole array is split into left side, current value, and right side, so knowing the total lets us compute the right side without a suffix array.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) extra

solutions.name: Reuse Output For Right Sums
solutions.description:
## Approach

First fill the output array with each index's right-side sum by scanning from right to left. Then scan left to right with a rolling left sum and overwrite each cell with the final difference.

## Key Insight

The answer array can temporarily store one side of the calculation, which avoids creating a separate suffix array while keeping the transformation easy to inspect.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
